title: North Sikkim with children and seniors
meta_description: Planning North Sikkim with kids or elders: the under-5 rule, which valley to pick, slower itineraries, altitude care, vehicles and family-friendly lodges.
summary: Children under 5 are not permitted in North Sikkim, so families with toddlers should plan elsewhere. For older children and healthy seniors, choose Lachung and Yumthang (3,564 m) over Gurudongmar, add nights in Gangtok or Dzongu before going up, use a comfortable SUV and keep Zero Point optional.

sections.heading: Start with the rules
paras: Two rules decide most family plans before anything else. Children under 5 are not permitted in North Sikkim protected areas, which means Lachung, Yumthang, Zero Point, Lachen, Thangu and Gurudongmar. Check posts ask for proof of age, so carry Aadhaar, a school ID with photo or a birth certificate for every child. And operators require a minimum of 2 nights in North Sikkim, with vehicles crossing the Toong check post by 4 pm, so the trip always includes two long drive days.

There is no upper age limit for seniors. What matters is health, fitness and how the trip is paced. In our experience, most healthy grandparents in their sixties and seventies enjoy Lachung and Yumthang very much, while Gurudongmar is a decision to take with their doctor. Check current status before you travel, because rules here have changed several times since 2023.

sections.heading: Which valley suits which family
paras: The simplest advice we give families: Lachung yes, Gurudongmar only if everyone is fit and well acclimatised.

sections.heading: Pace the trip slowly
paras: The most common mistake families make is arriving at Bagdogra in the morning and asking to be in Lachung that night. It is not possible because of the Toong 4 pm rule, and it would not be kind to anyone's body. Plan at least one night in Gangtok, at 1,650 m, before going north, and two if your flight lands after noon.

Our family itineraries take a slower ascent. A good shape for five nights is two nights in Gangtok, two in Lachung and one back in Gangtok. For families who want Gurudongmar, we add a night in Dzongu, at about 1,200 m, on the way up, and then two nights in Lachen before the lake. Three steps up instead of one jump makes a real difference to how children sleep and how seniors feel the next morning.

Keep each day light. One main outing per day is enough. Drive days of 5 to 7 hours from Gangtok are long for small bodies and stiff knees, so plan stops every 90 minutes: the Seven Sisters Waterfall, tea at Phodong, lunch near Mangan or Singhik, and the Naga Waterfall near Toong.

On the excursion morning, families do not need to leave at dawn with everyone else. Leaving Lachung at 7:30 or 8 am after a warm breakfast still gets you to Yumthang in good time on most days, and children are far happier for it. The trade-off is more cloud at Zero Point later in the morning, which matters less if you are not planning to go that high. Talk to your driver the evening before; most are happy to adjust for children and seniors.

sections.heading: Altitude care for young and old
paras: Children feel altitude like adults but often cannot describe it. Watch for crankiness, unusual sleepiness, loss of appetite, vomiting or a child who stops playing. Seniors may put breathlessness down to age and push on. In both cases the rule is the same: rest, water, no further climbing, and go down if it gets worse.

Keep everyone drinking 2 to 4 litres of water a day, warm if possible, and eat light, simple food. Avoid heavy meals before the high excursion. Dress children in more layers than you think they need, because they lose heat faster. At Zero Point or Gurudongmar, keep the visit to 20 to 30 minutes, and do not let children run in the snow at the top. If your doctor prescribes altitude medicine, follow their dose for children and seniors; do not use an adult's tablets.
list: Turn back if a child becomes listless, confused or keeps vomiting.
Turn back if a senior is breathless while sitting, or has chest pain.
Carry each person's regular medicines, with spare days in case a road closes.
Ask us for lodges with room heaters; cold nights disturb sleep for young and old.

sections.heading: Vehicles and lodges that work
paras: For families, the vehicle matters more than the hotel. A reserved Innova or Innova Crysta, rather than a shared Bolero, gives seniors proper seats with back support and lets you stop when a child needs a break. It costs roughly ₹3,000–5,000 more for a 2-night trip than a Scorpio, and we think it is worth every rupee on these roads. Shared-seat trips with fixed timings and cramped back benches are hard on families.

In Lachung, choose a lodge on the main road rather than one reached by steep steps, and ask for a ground or first-floor room. Rooms with a room heater, a geyser and an attached bathroom are worth paying a little more for. Lachen has fewer choices and simpler rooms, which is another reason to make Lachung the main North Sikkim base for families.

sections.heading: A sample 5-night family plan
paras: This is the shape we use most often for families with children over 5 and grandparents. It keeps the highest night at about 2,700 m and every drive day under seven hours.
list: Night 1, Gangtok: arrive from Bagdogra or NJP, about 124 km and 4.5–5 hours. Rest, short evening walk on MG Marg.
Night 2, Gangtok: gentle sightseeing such as Enchey Monastery, the ropeway and a view point. Permit documents go in today.
Night 3, Lachung: drive about 118 km in 5–7 hours with stops at the Seven Sisters Waterfall, Mangan and the Naga Waterfall. Early dinner.
Night 4, Lachung: Yumthang Valley after breakfast, not at dawn; Zero Point only if everyone is well. Afternoon rest and a walk to the monastery.
Night 5, Gangtok: drive back after a slow breakfast, arriving by late afternoon.
Day 6: transfer to Bagdogra or NJP for an afternoon or evening departure.

sections.heading: Food and comfort on the road
paras: Food in North Sikkim lodges is simple and filling: rice, dal, vegetables, egg or chicken, noodles and momos. Most children are happy, but bring familiar snacks, biscuits and fruit for the drives and the early starts. Tell your lodge in advance about vegetarian, Jain or other diets; most can manage with notice.

Toilets on the road are basic. Carry tissues, wet wipes and hand sanitiser. For seniors, a small cushion and a neck pillow make long drives more comfortable, and a walking stick helps on icy paths at Yumthang. A hot water bottle or two from Gangtok can rescue a cold night if the power goes.

sections.heading: If North Sikkim is not right this time
paras: If you have a child under 5, a family member with a serious heart or lung condition, or simply want an easier holiday, Sikkim has plenty at gentler heights. Gangtok and Rumtek, Pelling and Pemayangtse, Ravangla's Buddha Park, Namchi's Char Dham and a Dzongu homestay all sit below 2,200 m. Tsomgo Lake at about 3,750 m is a short half-day from Gangtok for those who want snow without a night up high. North Sikkim will still be there when the youngest turns five.
When you are ready, we will plan the North Sikkim leg around the slowest member of the family, not the fastest.

faqs.q: Can children under 5 go to North Sikkim?
faqs.a: No. Children under 5 are not permitted in North Sikkim protected areas, which include Lachung, Yumthang, Zero Point, Lachen and Gurudongmar. Check posts ask for proof of age. Families with toddlers can enjoy Gangtok, Rumtek, Pelling, Ravangla or Namchi instead. Check current status before you travel, as rules have changed before.

faqs.q: Is North Sikkim safe for senior citizens?
faqs.a: For healthy seniors, Lachung and Yumthang are usually very manageable with a night in Gangtok first and a comfortable SUV. The long drives tire more than the altitude. Gurudongmar at about 5,183 m is a decision to take with a doctor, and we advise against it for anyone with heart, lung or blood pressure problems.

faqs.q: Which is better for families, Lachung or Lachen?
faqs.a: Lachung. You sleep at about 2,700 m and visit Yumthang at 3,564 m, with Zero Point optional. Lachung also has more lodges with heaters and better rooms. Lachen exists mainly for Gurudongmar, a 4 am start to over 5,000 m, which suits fit adults and older teens better than young children or seniors.

faqs.q: What age do children need ID for North Sikkim?
faqs.a: Carry proof of age and identity for every child aged 5 and above: Aadhaar, a school ID with photo, a passport or a birth certificate. Check post staff compare faces and ages with the permit list, and a missing document can hold up the vehicle. Bring two passport photos per child for the permit application.

faqs.q: Can my parents go to Gurudongmar Lake?
faqs.a: If they are healthy and their doctor agrees, many seniors manage a short visit after two nights in Lachen. If they have heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, asthma or other lung conditions, we advise against it. A good compromise is for them to wait at Lachen or Thangu while the rest of the family goes.

faqs.q: How many days should a family plan for North Sikkim?
faqs.a: Plan at least five nights from Bagdogra: two in Gangtok, two in Lachung and one back in Gangtok. If you want Gurudongmar, make it six or seven nights with a night in Dzongu and two in Lachen. Short trips with long drive days are the main reason families come back exhausted.

faqs.q: Which vehicle is best for a family in North Sikkim?
faqs.a: A reserved Innova or Innova Crysta gives seniors proper seats and lets you stop when children need a break. It costs about ₹3,000–5,000 more for a 2-night trip than a Scorpio. Avoid shared-seat trips with families, because the timings are fixed and the back benches are cramped.

faqs.q: What are signs of altitude sickness in children?
faqs.a: Children often show altitude sickness as crankiness, unusual sleepiness, poor appetite, vomiting or simply stopping play, rather than saying they have a headache. If you notice these, rest, give water and do not climb further. If symptoms get worse, or the child is confused or very drowsy, go down at once and see a doctor.

faqs.q: Is Zero Point suitable for children?
faqs.a: Zero Point at about 4,700 m is a big jump from Lachung. Healthy older children often manage a short visit, but keep it to 20 to 30 minutes, dress them warmly and do not let them run. If a child seems unwell at Yumthang, skip Zero Point. Yumthang itself gives plenty of snow in winter.
